subject: Discrepancy in usage window / ratecard on June invoice
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@vertex-analytics.com>
To: paytech-support@paytech.com, david.kim@redwood.inference.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2026-06-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected rate change midbilling-window on June invoice

Hi team,

We just pulled our June invoice and noticed that for June 10-11 a subset of calls were billed at a higher per-token rate than the rest of the month. The product and finance teams tracked back to the request IDs and it looks like the same model/route. We do have a committed usage discount in place for the month, but the line items show a differential rate during that two-day window.

Can you explain why the ratecard changed mid-window and provide the usage log for 2026-06-10 to 2026-06-12 (UTC) so we can reconcile? Attached is our export of the invoice lines (vertex_invoice_lines_202606.csv).

We need a short explanation and any corrective credit before our July payroll close.

Thanks,
Marta
VP Finance
Vertex Analytics

Attachments: invoice_2026-06-01_2026-06-30.pdf (pdf), vertex_invoice_lines_202606.csv (csv)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@vertex-analytics.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com, laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2026-06-27T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected rate change midbilling-window on June invoice

Hi Marta — thanks for the flag and the CSV, really helpful.

Short answer: we don't change committed discount tiers mid-billing-window without a customer-authorized change, so this needs investigation. I'm opening an operational ticket to pull the canonical usage logs and the ratecard evaluation for your account for the 48-hour window.

Next steps from our side (I copied Rishi for billing escalation):
- I'll request per-request logs and the rate-evaluation trace for 2026-06-10 00:00:00 UTC through 2026-06-12 00:00:00 UTC.
- Rishi, can you confirm whether any rate overrides or manual adjustments were applied to Vertex Analytics account_id VERT-204 in that timeframe?
- Laura, if we find a billing error we should propose a corrective credit and a short note explaining the cause.

Marta — we'll aim to come back with the preliminary findings within 48 hours. If you need a faster turnaround, we can arrange a 30-minute call tomorrow.

Best,
David
Director, Customer Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
From: paytech-support@paytech.com
To: david.kim@redwood.inference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2026-06-28T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in usage window / ratecard on June invoice

Hi David / Rishi,

Attached are the exported audit logs and the rate-eval trace for VERT-204 covering 2026-06-09 through 2026-06-13 UTC. The rate-eval shows an override flag for 2026-06-10 03:14:22 UTC that propagated to a small subset of sessions. The override entry includes the operator who created it and a transient comment: "temp override to debug routing tests".

Attachment stubs:
- rate_eval_VERT-204_20260609-13.json (redacted)
- raw_request_log_VERT-204_20260609-13.csv

Notes: the override was not tied to a customer-initiated action; it appears to have been created by an engineer for internal routing testing and not flagged for rollback quickly enough. The number of affected requests is small (~6.3k tokens billed at the higher rate).

Let us know how you'd like that handled (credit + postmortem vs just credit).

Thanks,
PayTech Billing Ops
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@vertex-analytics.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com, laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2026-06-29T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in usage window / ratecard on June invoice

Marta — following up with the findings and proposal. Apologies for the inconvenience.

Summary of findings:
- Root cause: an internal rate override was applied by an engineer to test routing fallbacks; the override included a higher temporary rate and was unintentionally left active for ~4 hours on 2026-06-10.
- Impact: ~6,300 excess billed tokens (~$12.48 at displayed line-item rates). The override affected only the VERT-204 production route and did not alter committed-discount eligibility for the month.

Proposed remediation:
1) Immediate corrective credit for the exact overcharged amount ($12.48) to be applied to your July invoice.
2) A short postmortem (1-page) summarizing the operational gap and the corrective actions (policy: require two-person approval for rate overrides and an automatic rollback after 15 minutes unless extended).
3) Offer a one-time courtesy service credit of $100 since this impacted your reconciliation timeline.

Please confirm if Vertex is comfortable with the above remedy and whether we should issue the credit now or wait for any internal approvals on your side. Once you confirm, I'll route the credit through Finance and email you the updated invoice stub.

Again, sorry this slipped through — we will be updating our runbooks and adding additional monitoring alerts to prevent recurrence.

Best regards,
David
Director, Customer Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
